summary: Chromebook associates to duplicate SSID BSSID -> IPsec VPN disconnect and NAC re-auth blocks traffic
description:
Issue summary: Multiple users in the London office observed that Chromebooks (ChromeOS 114/115) suddenly lose corporate IPsec VPN (IKEv2) after connecting to an AP that shared the same SSID but different BSSID and VLAN. Impact: Users report immediate loss of service to internal tooling, console, GitHub repos and inability to reach internal KMS endpoints. Several sessions triggered NAC re-auth and received a restrictive ACL until manual rejoin.

Impact: Around 6 users in the office affected during the 09:00-10:30 window. Productivity blocked for a subset of platform engineers. Not customer-facing but high internal availability impact.

Environment: Office Wi-Fi: "RedwoodCorp-Employee" SSID, mixed 2.4/5GHz, controller: Aruba 8400; NAC: ISE 3.2; VPN gateway: Palo Alto GlobalProtect/IKEv2 terminating to FW cluster; DHCP via Catalyst DHCP relay; ChromeOS versions 114.x/115.x.

Observed after-change window: a new AP on temporary PoE switch was deployed earlier that morning. AP was mis-provisioned to the same VLAN tag as the guest AP but advertised the corporate SSID via a different BSSID.

Expected behavior: Devices should either: 1) choose the corporate AP with matching corporate VLAN and maintain VPN; or 2) if moved to a different VLAN, the client should drop and the NAC should present clear remediation steps rather than applying a restrictive ACL that blocks VPN control traffic.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Bring a ChromeOS laptop to the London office on a Wi-Fi profile bound to 'RedwoodCorp-Employee'.
2) Ensure two APs are broadcasting the SSID: one correctly configured on VLAN 100 (corporate) and one misconfigured on VLAN 300 (guest) but advertising same SSID.
3) Force assoc to the misconfigured AP (move physically closer or power-cycle the AP).
4) Observe IP assignment, default gateway and whether IKEv2 negotiations continue.
5) Check NAC session in ISE for posture and applied ACL.
observed_behavior: Immediately after associating to the misconfigured AP the Chromebook receives an IP from VLAN 300 (guest). IKE_SA rekey attempts fail: IKEv2 SA tears down with CHILD_SA negotiation errors, then ChromeOS initiates rekey which times out. NAC (ISE) detects mismatch and applies a restrictive ACL; device loses both internal and internet-bound access to corporate endpoints. Users cannot trigger a transparent reauth; manual disconnect/reconnect to the correct AP is required.\n\nNetwork evidence: DHCP offered from wrong scope (10.30.0.0/24) rather than corporate (10.10.0.0/24). IKE logs show error 'NO_PROPOSAL_CHOSEN' followed by 'ISAKMP-SA not found' and rekey timeouts.
expected_behavior: Client should either get corporate VLAN and keep VPN alive, or, if VLAN difference detected, NAC should redirect to onboarding/remediation page rather than apply a full block that prevents reauth. VPN gateway should fallback gracefully or clearly report misconfiguration so SRE/network team can detect earlier.
logs: IKE logs (vpn-gw-02) 2026-03-10T09:12:14Z: 'peer 10.30.12.45:500 IKE_SA_INIT received', 2026-03-10T09:12:15Z: 'NO_PROPOSAL_CHOSEN', 2026-03-10T09:12:16Z: 'CHILD_SA negotiation failed' ; DHCP server dhcp-srv-lon.log excerpt: 'DISCOVER from 24:6E:96:AB:CD:EF; OFFER to 24:6E:96:AB:CD:EF via 10.30.0.12 scope 10.30.0.0/24'; ISE session trace: 'AuthZ decision: RESTRICTIVE_ACL applied due to VLAN-mismatch posture'. Full packet capture uploaded: https://s3.redwood-inference.internal/network/pcaps/INT-76321-chrome-ike-pcap.pcap
temporary_workaround: Network team instructed to power-cycle the misprovisioned AP and remove the SSID from the guest VLAN. Users were advised to toggle Wi-Fi off/on and re-select the corporate AP; manual reauth performed via ISE guest portal allowed restore. For immediate mitigation we disabled fast roaming 802.11r on nearby APs to reduce client flapping until patch deployed.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:35 - Support (Aisha Malik): User reported laptop 'lost VPN and couldn't access console'. Collected ChromeOS system logs and DHCP lease details.
2026-03-10 09:48 - Network Eng (Jorge Ramirez): Correlated with new AP deployment in rack R1. Confirmed a radio was mistakenly mapped to VLAN 300 while advertising corporate SSID.

2026-03-10 10:02 - Security (Priya Desai): ISE shows posture change triggered by VLAN mismatch; recommended failing soft-landing to onboarding portal rather than ACL block. Opening follow-up policy ticket.
2026-03-10 10:25 - User (Evan Cho): Confirmed reconnect to correct AP regained VPN and internal resources; requested automate detection to avoid future manual fixes.
2026-03-11 14:12 - Network Eng (Jorge Ramirez): Applied firmware patch to AP image and updated provisioning template. Will monitor for recurrence and file change in config management.
investigation_notes:
Hypothesis: SSID/BSSID collision + VLAN misassignment causing IP change mid-IKE life-cycle. ChromeOS expects continuous connectivity; sudden subnet/gateway change causes IKE SA validation to fail and client attempts rekey from new source IP, which the VPN gateway rejects. ISE treats the new IP as non-corporate and enforces restrictive ACL.

Evidence collected: DHCP leases, AP provisioning snapshot, ISE session traces, and pcap showing IKE_INIT from 10.30.x.x then NAT detection mismatch. No indication of DNS poisoning or intentional spoofing.

Next steps: Add an AP provisioning validation script to CI to prevent corporate SSID assignment on guest VLANs. Add a monitoring alert to detect corporate SSID broadcasting in guest VLANs (controller syslog). Investigate whether VPN gateway can tolerate source-IP change mid-session (suggested feature request to firewall vendor).
resolution: Workaround implemented: misconfig AP removed from rack, provisioning template fixed. Firmware patched to prevent mismatched VLAN assignment on SSID profiles. ISE policy updated to present an onboarding/reauth portal when VLAN mismatch posture detected instead of immediate restrictive ACL. Follow-up action: Create configuration validation check in Ansible templates and add a dashboard alert for corporate-SSID-on-noncorporate-VLAN events. Pending: vendor feature request to accept transient IP change for IKE rekey (ticket opened with firewall vendor).
notes_for_postmortem: Recommend adding a short postmortem that includes timeline, root cause, mitigation, and three engineering action items: (1) provisioning validation CI check, (2) monitoring alert, (3) NAC policy UX change to clear remediation flow.
